definition_text: BSI was defined as the isolation of a bacterial pathogen from at least one set of blood cultures (one aerobic and one anaerobic) drawn from a transplant recipient either from the day of starting PTCY or from the day of the stem cell infusion for patients receiving other prophylaxis, to long-term follow-up. All BSI episodes were confirmed after reviewing clinical charts. To define a BSI as that caused by a common skin colonizer such as coagulase-negative staphylococci or Corynebacterium, we required a suggestive clinical presentation and (i) >=2 blood cultures drawn from different sites, (ii) >=1 positive blood culture obtained from the peripheral vein blood and a positive catheter culture. Those patients with any positive culture that was considered a contaminant were included in the group of not-infected patients. Polymicrobial infection was defined when the BSI was caused by 2 or more different microorganisms. Only the first episode of BSI was counted as an event.

extraction_notes: Sensitivity timepoint = end of study follow-up (censored at 18 months/543 days). Rate 7.8% reported directly in narrative text. Event count from Table 2 sums to 6, consistent with 6/77=7.8%.
